hypotheses.paper: B a quotient of an open subset Omega of M^n by a group of isometries acting freely and properly discontinuously (l.1836-1838)
hypotheses.note: this hypothesis is now formalized: FlatQuotient Gamma Omega under [Invariant Gamma Omega] [IsCancelSMul Gamma Omega] [ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul Gamma Omega], and IsQuotientOf M Gamma Omega; the lemma itself (linear twisted product) is not attempted here

prose_items.item: quotients Gamma\Omega of open subsets of M^n (l.209-211, l.610-612, l.1204-1208, l.1279, l.1836-1838)
prose_items.status: closed for the construction (T2, covering, (Isom, M^n)-atlas, local isometry, IsQuotientOf, connectedness); partial for the descent of Cauchy surfaces (needs ActsAcausally); hypotheses of the descent inhabited by the nontrivial spacelike translation group spaceGroup (barbotGH_spaceGroup)

findings_general: Freeness and proper discontinuity do not make Gamma\Omega causal: Z e0 (a timelike translation) acts freely and properly discontinuously on M^n and Z e0\M^n is a non-causal flat spacetime (not_isCausal_timeGroup). Barbot never claims otherwise; every quotient he calls GH carries a Gamma-invariant time function (l.1184-1187) or Cauchy surface. Any lemma of the form 'quotient of GH is GH' must carry a hypothesis on the action.

The descent of Cauchy surfaces (l.1207-1208, 'level sets ... are Cauchy hypersurfaces which are quotients Gamma\S_t') is proved under ActsAcausally (no gamma != 1 and x with x <= gamma x in Omega). In the paper's setting (a Gamma-invariant regular cosmological time, l.1184-1187) this holds because that time is strictly increasing along <=; the library's IsTimeFunction (DEC-10, strict on << only) does not give it, so the implication is not one lemma away in the library's vocabulary. An achronal action (no x << gamma x) would not suffice for the argument (null translations). The hypotheses are inhabited by Z e1 (a spacelike translation of Minkowski (d+1), l.209-211): barbotGH_spaceGroup.
Causality of Gamma\Omega under ActsAcausally is not proved: it needs the lifting of the <= relation on the top open set of the quotient, not only of causal curves.
kb_proposals: Quotients Gamma\Omega: put [Invariant Gamma Omega] (a class) on Omega : Opens (Minkowski d); then the action instance, mathlib's T2 instance and mathlib's MulAction.instChartedSpaceQuotient all fire on FlatQuotient Gamma Omega (an abbrev for MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient); atlas members destructure with `obtain ⟨q, rfl⟩ := he` and IsLocalHomeomorph.localInverseAt_symm reads them.

A map sending each point of Omega into its own Gamma-orbit, continuous at p0, is locally one gamma (FlatQuotient.eventually_eq_smul): the one lemma behind both HasGroupoid of the quotient and the local isometry of the projection.

Lifting causal curves through a covering: an interval subtype is contractible (Convex.contractibleSpace) and locally path-connected (private locPathConnectedSpace_of_ordConnected, via LocPathConnectedSpace.of_bases and IsPathConnected.preimage_coe), so IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts applies; causality of the lift is local, through LocalIsomorphism.

Inextensibility (DEC-11/13, the 'grows' clause is about images) lifts through a covering by the argument here (inextensible_of_lift) when no two points of one orbit lie on one causal curve: carry ActsAcausally. Necessity is not established (plausible for d = 0, where Z e0\M^1 is a circle a curve over [0,1) already covers; for d >= 1 an extension can usually leave in a new direction).
